newsitem.title: CHINA: Graft battle prevents losses at China's Shougang.
newsitem.headline: Graft battle prevents losses at China's Shougang.

text.p: China's Capital Iron and Steel, or Shougang Group, has dealt with 68 economic crimes, preventing 24.02 million yuan in losses in the past two years, the Procuratorial Daily said on Wednesday.

The newspaper hailed the success of the struggle against corruption launched by Shougang authorities since Zhou Guanwu resigned as chairman and Communist Party secretary of Beijing's largest steel works in February 1995 after the arrest of his son, Zhou Beifang.

Zhou Beifang, head of Shougang's Hong Kong subsidiaries Shougang Concord International Enterprises and Shougang Concord Grand, was given a suspended death sentence late last year for taking bribes totalling HK$9.28 million ($1.2 million) and paying 1.2 million yuan ($144,6000) in bribes.
In 1996, Shougang officials handed in 99,000 yuan worth of gifts and company authorities punished 15 officials for abusing public funds, the newspaper said but gave no further details.

The Shougang Group produced 7.92 million tonnes of steel, 7.92 million tonnes of rolled steel and 7.3 million tonnes of iron in 1996 and generated a pre-tax profit of 324 million yuan ($39.0 million).
